thread:
dan (Eng): Quick one  our US team is on company shutdown 12/24-12/27 but my teammate in APAC (on sabbatical return) asked if they can bank one statutory holiday from their country into a holiday bank because they'll be on unpaid sabbatical for 4 weeks overlapping the shutdown. is that possible?

oliver (People Ops): short answer: maybe. we distinguish between floating holidays (employee-level) and statutory holiday banks (local entitlements). people on unpaid sabbatical generally don't accrue new PTO during leave, but handling pre-existing statutory days varies by legal entity. what country is your teammate in?

dan (Eng): singapore. they had a statutory day (hari nasional) that fell during sabbatical window and want to avoid losing it.

maya (HR): singapore law: employees are entitled to statutory public holidays, but entitlement during unpaid leave depends on local contract. if the day falls while they're on unpaid leave, it's usually forfeited unless contract or local policy says otherwise. some companies maintain a "holiday bank" for return-to-work adjustments. we can do an exception if payroll & benefits approve and there's legal support.

emma (Payroll): operational note: to bank a statutory day we need: manager approval screenshot, employee signed consent, and an HR legal signoff. payroll must be notified before the monthly payroll cutoff (12/10 for December) to reflect in year-end reporting. otherwise bookkeeping will show it as forfeited and we'd need a manual JV.

sabrina (Benefits): benefits perspective: if we bank the day we record it as an "earned but deferred" day on rehiring/return. this affects accrual calculations for the next period. also check whether banked days can be taken as paid time off within 6 months of return per local practice. if employee will be unpaid for >30 days we often treat statutory days as non-accruing unless exception approved.

dan (Eng): got it. what's the process to request exception?

oliver (People Ops): steps: 1) manager posts approval in thread (dan pls). 2) employee signs consent form (we can DM them the template). 3) people-ops files Legal intake for SG jurisdiction. 4) payroll receives approval + legal memo before 12/10 cutoff. we'll provide a decision within 3 business days of intake.

dan (Eng): i approve. i'll ask teammate to sign.

maya (HR): quick template note for record: "I consent to bank my statutory public holiday that falls during my unpaid sabbatical for future use upon my return." include dates and employee signature.

emma (Payroll): once we get the signed consent and legal signoff i'll tag Finance to post the deferred pay entry. be aware that if the employee later requests payout instead of time off we need a separate approval from Finance.

timebot: reminder set for 2026-11-30: submit legal intake for cross-region holiday bank requests before payroll cutoff.

sabrina (Benefits): small policy addendum: this is an exception-heavy area. if multiple people in the same country request booking we should consider a local policy update. ping people-ops before group requests.

dan (Eng): thanks team. i'll coordinate with the teammate and loop back here once signed. :pray:

oliver (People Ops): resolving for now pending docs. ping if you need the consent template or legal contact. :white_check_mark:
